```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4.5)
```

```{r}
library(pgmcompR)
```

Exact inference is exponential in the treewidth of the model. When that is
too large, approximate methods trade exactness for speed. Every approximate
result in pgmcompR carries class `pgm_approximate` and a diagnostics
attribute, so it cannot be mistaken for an exact answer.

```{r}
sp <- example_network("sprinkler")
exact <- query(sp, "Rain", list(WetGrass = "T"))
exact
```

## Forward sampling and rejection

```{r}
r <- query(sp, "Rain", list(WetGrass = "T"), method = "rejection", n = 20000, seed = 1)
r
attr(r, "diagnostics")$acceptance_rate
```

Rejection sampling discards every sample that disagrees with the evidence,
so it becomes useless when the evidence is unlikely.

## Likelihood weighting and importance sampling

Likelihood weighting clamps the evidence and weights each sample by the
likelihood of the evidence. The effective sample size (ESS) shows how much
the weights degrade the sample.

```{r}
lw <- query(sp, "Rain", list(WetGrass = "T"), method = "likelihood_weighting", n = 20000, seed = 1)
lw
```

General importance sampling draws from a proposal network with the same
graph and states:

```{r}
proposal <- add_cpd(sp, cpd("Rain", c(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 0.8), "Cloudy", list(Rain = c("F", "T"), Cloudy = c("F", "T"))))
query(sp, "Rain", list(WetGrass = "T"), method = "importance", proposal = proposal, n = 20000, seed = 1)
```

## Gibbs sampling

Gibbs sampling resamples each unobserved variable from its full conditional
given its Markov blanket. Several chains are run; the split R-hat, bulk ESS
and Monte Carlo standard error (MCSE) follow Vehtari et al. (2021).

```{r}
gb <- query(sp, "Rain", list(WetGrass = "T"), method = "gibbs", n = 3000,
            chains = 4, burn_in = 500, seed = 2)
gb
d <- attr(gb, "diagnostics")
d$rhat
d$ess
```

Deterministic CPDs (zeros) can make a Gibbs chain reducible. R-hat well
above 1.01 signals that the chains have not mixed; a warning of class
`pgm_convergence_warning` is raised.

## Loopy belief propagation

On a tree shaped factor graph, belief propagation is exact. On a graph with
cycles it is an approximation that may oscillate; damping helps.

```{r}
cancer <- example_network("cancer")
belief_propagation(cancer, list(Xray = "positive"))$exact
loopy <- loopy_bp(sp, list(WetGrass = "T"), damping = 0.5)
loopy
```

`belief_propagation()` refuses to run on a loopy graph unless
`allow_loops = TRUE`, so an approximate result is always explicitly
requested.

## Comparing methods

```{r}
methods <- c("rejection", "likelihood_weighting", "gibbs", "loopy_bp")
est <- vapply(methods, function(m) {
  q <- suppressWarnings(query(sp, "Rain", list(WetGrass = "T"), method = m, n = 5000, seed = 3))
  factor_values(q)[2]
}, numeric(1))
round(c(exact = factor_values(exact)[2], est), 4)
```

## Reproducibility

The `seed` argument makes a call reproducible without changing the global
random number stream of the session.
